citeAs: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari (2024). Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562.
creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari (University of Texas at Austin, Microsoft, University of Colorado Boulder)
description: VQAonline is the first Visual Question Answering dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case, sourced from the Stack Exchange online question-answering platform. It contains 64,696 VQAs with authentic questions, images, context, and answers validated by the question askers, spanning 105 diverse topics. Answers are notably longer than in prior VQA datasets, with a mean of 173 words.
name: VQAonline
publisher: University of Texas at Austin; Microsoft; University of Colorado Boulder
rai:annotationsPerItem: For user intention annotation: 2 independent annotations per VQA, with a 3rd annotation for tie-breaking (for 25 out of 105 cases). For human evaluation of model outputs: 6 model-generated answers rated per VQA by one domain expert each.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers for user intention annotation: located in the United States, completed more than 500 HITs with over 95% approval rating on Amazon Mechanical Turk. Domain experts for human evaluation: ten individuals each with at least a Master's degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic, located in the United States.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention taxonomy development, two annotators conducted four rounds of analysis on 105 visual questions. Agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa improved from 45.24% to 84.69% across rounds. For human evaluation quality control, the median and mean times per model answer assessment were 1.4 and 1.29 minutes respectively.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for user intention annotation); custom home-grown web-based interface (for domain expert human evaluation)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For user intention annotation: crowdworkers were provided instructions, taxonomy definitions, and two examples per user intention category. Each worker received one-on-one Zoom training and passed a qualifying annotation test. Two independent workers (A and B) annotated each of 105 VQAs; when they disagreed (25 out of 105), a third worker (C) broke the tie. For human evaluation of model outputs: ten domain experts (each with at least a Master's degree) rated model-generated answers as incorrect (0), partially correct (0.5), or correct (1) for 20 VQAs each across 10 topics.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Internet. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, Europe and less from countries like Egypt. The dataset has a long-tail distribution across topics, with as few as 10 examples in some topics and over 20,000 in others. Most visual questions are in English.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by scraping the Stack Exchange online question-answering platform. All examples containing four components were collected: a natural language question (post "title"), a natural language context (post "body"), an image (URL link), and at least one accepted answer. Only examples where the question poster marked an "accepted answer" were included. Data spanned from August 2010 to November 2022.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided URL link were removed from the dataset. This step reduced the dataset from 65,849 to 64,696 visual questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data from Stack Exchange archive in XML format, consisting of posts with titles (questions), body text (context), image URLs, and answers. The archive is hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange. The initial candidate pool was 330,705 visual questions before filtering.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas. Geographic representation is unbalanced. Answers are considerably longer (mean 173 words) than existing VQA datasets, making standard VQA evaluation metrics ill-suited. Most benchmarked models are believed to have been trained on Stack Exchange data, potentially contaminating evaluation. The dataset excludes 75 technology topics (e.g., Stack Overflow, LaTeX) because they typically involve language/code problems.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two filtering steps were applied: (1) removed low-quality VQAs with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer based on Stack Exchange's up-vote/down-vote system; (2) excluded visual questions with multiple images (e.g., GIFs) or with visual answers. Additionally, examples for which the image could not be downloaded were removed. All images were converted to PNG format for data format consistency.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Improved models designed for VQAonline can benefit many real-world applications including other community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, as well as visual search and browsing. The dataset facilitates research into hallucination issues in authentic use cases.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking VQA models on authentic use cases; evaluating long-form answer generation; research into community question answering platforms; improving VQA models for real-world applications including virtual assistants, visual dialog, visual search, and learning assistance tools for children; studying hallucination in vision-language models; multilingual VQA research.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5 was used to bootstrap user intention categories via zero-shot prompting. DeepSolo (state-of-the-art text spotter model) was used to detect text presence in all images in the dataset. LLaMA2 was used as an evaluation metric to rate model-generated answers.

null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described; missing images led to removal of examples rather than imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation, augmentation, or resampling is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The evidence quote does not actually discuss personal/sensitive information handling — it only describes how data was collected from Stack Exchange. The paper does not explicitly discuss PII or sensitive information in the dataset.

evidence.name: We introduce the first VQA dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums, we call it VQAonline.
evidence.description: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange. We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022, and adhered to all data license restrictions (cc-by-sa 4.0) set forth by Stack Exchange.
evidence.url: To encourage community-wide progress, we publicly-share the dataset at https://vqaonline.github.io/.

evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Stack Exchange data is hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format. We started with 330,705 candidate visual questions. After removing visual questions without an accepted answer, it resulted in 165,766 visual questions.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We conducted two filtering steps to obtain our final dataset of 64,696 VQAs. First, we removed low-quality VQAs based on Stack Exchange's feature that enables users to up-vote or down-vote each post. We removed visual questions with scores 0 or less for either the question or answer. Second, we excluded visual questions with multiple images (e.g., GIF) or with visual answers. Finally, after removing examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link, we got to our final dataset of 64,696 visual questions. For data format consistency, we converted all images to png form
evidence.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Finally, after removing examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link, we got to our final dataset of 64,696 visual questions.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We provided instructions, taxonomy definitions, and two examples per user intention category. The annotation task interface showed for each visual question the question, context, and answer. To facilitate collecting high-quality results, we provided each crowdworker with one-on-one Zoom training. We also provided a qualifying annotation test that all workers passed to verify they understood the instructions.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: We hired three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk to perform our task. For quality control, we only accepted workers located in the United States who had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating.
evidence.rai:annotationsPerItem: To enable the assessment of high-quality results, we collected two user intention annotations from two independent workers (worker A and B) per VQA instance (i.e. image-question-context-answer) for 105 randomly selected VQAs, one from each of 105 topics. We then detected if their annotations matched. We found that 25 out of 105 didn't match. Thus, we hired a third worker (worker C) to break the tie.
evidence.rai:annotatorDemographics: We hired three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk to perform our task. For quality control, we only accepted workers located in the United States who had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating. We hired ten domain experts to represent each of the ten fields (topics). To guarantee English proficiency, as most of our visual questions are written in English, we only accepted experts located in the United States.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: We observed slight agreement accuracy improvement and Cohen's kappa agreement improvement after each round. Specifically, from round 1 to round 4, agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa agreement improved from 45.24% to 84.69%.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Despite the VQAonline dataset's inclusion of multilingual VQAs and coverage of users' generated visual questions from various countries, we highlight that this dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Internet. Additionally, the geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, Europe and less from countries like Egypt.

Additionally, the geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, Europe and less from countries like Egypt.

Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, as well as visual search and browsing. To encourage community-wide progress, we publicly-share the dataset at https://vqaonline.github.io/.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We first brainstormed 11 free-form user intention categories. To do so, we solicited help from GPT-3.5 by having it indicate via a zero-shot prompt the user intentions when given a question and context. We conducted text spotting model to determine the presence of text within the images. We utilized the state-of-the-art text spotter model DeepSolo to detect text for all images in our dataset.
evidence.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Originally, this information was collected from Stack Exchange users via four user entry interactions. The natural language question was collected as the post "title", using a text entry field paired with instructions "be specific and imagine you're asking a question to another person" when writing the question.
